title: Jitney dance halls and the Astoria band with Lee Collins and David Jones
summary: He takes John Marrero's banjo job at the La Vila jitney dance hall, then joins Lee Collins, David Jones and John Robichaud at the Astoria, where Albert Morgan joins on bass and Don Albert arrives.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: Budweiser? Was it near the Budweiser?

Well, maybe this was the fern, it was the Budweiser and the fern, they were right next to each other. The Vila was the La Vila? La Vila, that's it, that's it. Yeah. John Maria had charge of that job, and he had... It was his job, John Maria to banjo. Well, like I said, I used to always go around, you see. In fact, I can tell you, there's a different place, they had a different place on St. Charles and Cronolette. They had one on Burgundy and Canal. And then, like you said, the La Vila and the Vila were right next to each other, you see. Well, and often, you go around those places and you'd say, well, I ain't doing, I'm not doing anything. So I used to go around with La Vila and John, and then those guys were particularly who they'd let play, because if you wasn't a good player, they wouldn't let you play, you see. So I'd go around there and arrest John up a while, and John would go and steal Howard. So, well, the guys wouldn't worry because they knew I could hold a job down. Well, in that band was Joe Robichaud on piano, Thero Poitain on alto, and Albert Martin, we call them Fats on drums. Is that right? Yeah, they didn't use no bass in those bands. No, they didn't use no bass, no. Look at that. I see it. Lee Collins on trumpet, Thero on alto sax, and Joe Rocha on piano, and Fats on drum, and John Murray on banjo. Yeah. So John was going to New York, you see. And there was another fella named Willie Conray. Willie Conray. Well, like John, like I said, he was the idle banjo player at that time. And everybody used to like to copy. I myself used to copy behind him, you see. And there was another Willie Conray. Willie Conray, I found I was supposed to get that job too. But anyhow, the job finally came to me. And at that same time, they had hired David Jones. They put David, they had, in other words, the guy had so much fluent with the proprietor. Beansley wanted to have a club, want to have a nightclub on Astoria, and they had a show here, that was stranded, a full good show. I think the lyrics must have been running them days. And so when we got the job, and we built up a terrific band there. With those, let's say, and that band, I believe, Albert Morgan, that's how we put Albert Morgan on bass, yeah.
